slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: Uricase oxidises uric acid to allantoin and hydrogen peroxide.
With POD, H2O2, 4-aminophenazone and dichlorophenol sulfonate (DCPS) form a red quinoneimine; the colour is proportional to the uric acid concentration.
Uric acid is the end product of purine metabolism; a rise may point to renal failure and is commonly associated with gout.

This protocol follows, as an example, the instructions for use of the SPINREACT “Uric acid” kit (IFU BSIS01-I, 04/02/16). The IFU of your laboratory’s own kit always takes precedence: other kits may use different volumes, times, factors and reference values.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Specimen: serum or plasma — stable 3–5 days at 2–8 °C or 6 months at −20 °C.
24-hour urine: stable 4 days at 15–25 °C (pH > 8); dilute 1/50 and multiply the result by 50. Warm cloudy urine to 60 °C for 10 min; do not refrigerate.
R1 (buffer): phosphate pH 7.4 50 mmol/L, DCPS 4 mmol/L. R2 (enzymes): uricase 60 U/L, POD 660 U/L, ascorbate oxidase 200 U/L, 4-aminophenazone 1 mmol/L. Standard: 6 mg/dL.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Equipment: spectrophotometer or analyser reading at 520 nm, 1.0 cm cuvettes.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: Working reagent: dissolve one vial of R2 in one bottle of R1; cap and mix gently.
Working reagent stability: 1 month at 2–8 °C or 10 days at room temperature.
Store the kit at 2–8 °C protected from light; particles or turbidity are signs of deterioration.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.
The values come from the SPINREACT “Uric acid” IFU (BSIS01-I). The IFU of the kit you use and the analyser manual always take precedence — check the programme against them.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 1. Conditions: wavelength 520 nm (490–550); temperature 37 °C or 15–25 °C.
2. Use a 1 cm cuvette; zero the instrument with distilled water.
3. Pipette into a cuvette: blank — working reagent 1.0 mL; standard — working reagent 1.0 mL + standard 25 µL; sample — working reagent 1.0 mL + sample 25 µL.
4. Mix and incubate: 5 min at 37 °C or 10 min at 15–25 °C.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 5. Read the absorbance (A) of the sample and standard against the blank; the colour is stable for at least 30 minutes.

slides.title: Semi-automatic analyser: uric acid programme
rows: Sample and standard — against the reagent blank

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: Result (mg/dL) = (A sample − A blank) / (A standard − A blank) × 6 (standard concentration).
24-hour urine: result × urine volume (dL/24 h) = mg/24 h. Conversion: mg/dL × 59.5 = µmol/L.
Linear up to 40 mg/dL; above that, dilute the sample 1/2 with NaCl 9 g/L and multiply the result by 2.

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: IFU reference: women 2.5–6.8 mg/dL (149–405 µmol/L), men 3.6–7.7 mg/dL (214–458 µmol/L); urine 250–750 mg/24 h.
These values are for orientation; each laboratory should establish its own reference range.

slides.title: Interferences and errors
bullets: Bilirubin up to 170 µmol/L, haemoglobin up to 130 mg/dL and ascorbic acid up to 570 µmol/L do not interfere.
The standard is easily contaminated — use clean disposable tips.
IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.

slides.title: Interferences and errors
bullets: Drugs and other interfering substances are listed in the literature (IFU — Young DS).
IFU: performance depends on the analyser used.

slides.title: Quality control
bullets: Assayed control sera are run with each series (IFU: SPINTROL H Normal and Pathologic).
If a control falls outside its range, check the instrument, reagents and calibrator; do not release patient results.
Each laboratory sets its own quality-control scheme and the corrective actions when controls are out of tolerance.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: Serum and plasma are potentially infectious: wear gloves and never pipette by mouth.
Follow the precautions in the IFU and the safety data sheet (SDS) when handling the reagents.
Used cuvettes, tubes and tips are disinfected.
